chunks: Hadith 2318 — Abū Hammām Ismāʿīl ibn Hammām narrated from al-Riḍā عليه السلام that he said:
To a man: “What do you understand sakīnah to be?” The people did not know what it was, so they said, “May Allah make us your ransom, what is it?”

He said: “It is a breeze that comes forth from Paradise, fragrant, having a form like the form of a human being. It is with the Prophets عليهم السلام, and it is that which was sent down upon Ibrāhīm عليه السلام when he built the Kaʿbah. Then it began indicating this way and that way, and he built the foundation upon it.”

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Prophet Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, upon whom the sakīnah descended when building the Kaʿbah
key_terms.السَّكِينَةُ: sakīnah; a divinely sent tranquility or presence explained here as a fragrant breeze from Paradise
key_terms.الْأَسَاسَ: the foundation established upon the guidance indicated by the sakīnah
key_terms.الْأَنْبِيَاءِ: the Prophets, with whom this sakīnah remains
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, the source from which this sakīnah comes forth
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةَ: the Kaʿbah, whose foundation was built with the guidance of the sakīnah
key_terms.رِيحٌ: a breeze or wind issuing from Paradise

ai.seo_question: What does sakīnah mean in Shia hadith, and how was it connected to Prophet Ibrāhīm عليه السلام building the Kaʿbah?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the meaning of sakīnah as a fragrant breeze from Paradise with a human-like form that accompanies the Prophets عليهم السلام. It identifies this sakīnah as what descended upon Ibrāhīm عليه السلام during the building of the Kaʿbah and guided the placement of its foundations. The report serves as a Quranic commentary on the concept of sakīnah and links it to sacred history and divine support for the Prophets.
